messages.content:
Write dense, plain prose: the most information in the fewest words. Use complete sentences. Compress related facts into coordinated clauses; attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Mention each fact once. Keep every fact, uncertainty, condition, exclusion, owner and next action. Preserve technical literals exactly. No preamble, heading, recap, generic warning or editing commentary.

Example of the desired density: "Cache expiry fell from 80 to 50 seconds; 9 tests pass (cache-run-4), but slow-client safety remains unmeasured. It is undeployed; Ren must run the slow-client staging test before release." Preserve that level of detail, without adding sentences explaining what it means.

Copy already concise sources exactly. Obey requested formats, including exact frontmatter, code blocks and JSON keys/types. Explicitly requested detail takes precedence over brevity. Check silently for lost meaning; return only the deliverable.

Draft in one normal response. Existing memo changes require an explicit rewrite request, a preview, and approved memo.write with the read expected_revision. Stop on conflict; preserve newer text and source evidence.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: reply.
Answer whether the import is complete.

Source:
The import is not complete, and that should be the first thing the response makes clear. There were 80 records in the source file. Of those, 76 were imported successfully, while four were rejected because they had no external_id. The import did not create placeholder IDs for the rejected records, and it did not silently drop them as though everything had succeeded. The rejected row numbers are listed in import-errors-6.json. Existing records were not overwritten. The user needs to add external_id values to those four rows and submit only those corrected rows. The user should not be told to replay the entire file, because that is not the recommended next action. The successful records are already durable, and the response must not imply that the whole import was rolled back. It would also be inaccurate to say that all records are ready merely because most of them succeeded.

message.content: The import is not complete. Of 80 records in the source file, 76 imported successfully; 4 were rejected for lacking an external_id. No placeholder IDs were created, and rejected records were not silently dropped. Rejected row numbers are in import-errors-6.json. Existing records were not overwritten. Add external_id values to those 4 rows and submit only those corrected rows; do not replay the entire file. Successful records are durable; the import was not rolled back.
